extracted.intended_audience: public water system operators, state regulators, and drinking water compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory criteria from 40 CFR Part 141 (Subparts including H, L, etc.) specifying maximum contaminant levels, treatment technique requirements, best available technologies, monitoring and operational requirements for public water systems (surface water and ground water under direct influence of surface water).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total coliform MCL (presence/absence basis until Mar 31, 2016)
rubrics_metrics.description: Until March 31, 2016, the total coliform MCL is based on the presence or absence of total coliforms in a sample, rather than coliform density.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For systems collecting at least 40 samples/month: no more than 5.0 percent of samples in a month may be total coliform-positive. For systems collecting fewer than 40 samples/month: no more than one sample/month may be total coliform-positive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total coliform MCL violation conditions (repeat positives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Until March 31, 2016, any fecal coliform-positive repeat sample or E. coli-positive repeat sample, or any total coliform-positive repeat sample following a fecal coliform-positive or E. coli-positive routine sample, constitutes a violation of the MCL for total coliforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For public notification purposes (subpart Q), this is a violation that may pose an acute risk to health.

rubrics_metrics.name: E. coli MCL compliance beginning April 1, 2016
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning April 1, 2016, a system is in compliance with the MCL for E. coli for samples taken under subpart Y unless specified conditions occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation of the MCL may pose an acute risk to health. The listed conditions that cause noncompliance are: (1) an E. coli-positive repeat sample following a total coliform-positive routine sample; (2) a total coliform-positive repeat sample following an E. coli-positive routine sample; (3) failure to take all required repeat samples following an E. coli-positive routine sample; (4) failure to test for E. coli when any repeat sample tests positive for total coliform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly compliance determination for coliforms/E. coli
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine compliance with the MCL for total coliforms (prior to April 1, 2016) or E. coli (beginning April 1, 2016) for each month in which the system is required to monitor for total coliforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must apply the appropriate paragraph ((a)/(b) prior to 2016; (c) after 2016) to each monitoring month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best technologies/treatment techniques for total coliforms and E. coli
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator identifies technologies/treatment techniques/other means available for achieving compliance with the MCL for total coliforms and E. coli.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed measures: (1) Protection of wells from fecal contamination by appropriate placement and construction; (2) Maintenance of a disinfectant residual throughout the distribution system; (3) Proper maintenance of the distribution system including pipe replacement and repair, main flushing, storage tank/reservoir operation and maintenance, cross connection control, and maintaining positive pressure; (4) Filtration and/or disinfection of surface water (subparts H, P, T, W) or disinfection of ground water (subpart S) using strong oxidants such as chlorine, chlorine dioxide, or ozone; (5) For ground water systems, compliance with an EPA-approved State Wellhead Protection Program under section 1428 of the SDWA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affordable technologies identification for small systems (≤10,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator identifies the technologies/treatment techniques/other means in the preceding paragraph as affordable for systems serving 10,000 or fewer people for achieving compliance with total coliform and E. coli MCLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCLs for bromate and chlorite
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum contaminant levels for bromate and chlorite: Bromate 0.010 mg/L; Chlorite 1.0 mg/L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance dates: CWSs and NTNCWSs in Subpart H serving ≥10,000 persons must comply beginning Jan 1, 2002; serving <10,000 persons and groundwater-only systems not under direct influence must comply beginning Jan 1, 2004. Best available technologies: Bromate—control of ozone treatment process to reduce bromate production; Chlorite—control of treatment processes to reduce disinfectant demand and control of disinfection treatment processes to reduce disinfectant levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCLs for TTHM and HAA5 (Subpart L RAA compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLs: Total trihalomethanes (TTHM) 0.080 mg/L; Haloacetic acids (five) (HAA5) 0.060 mg/L. Subpart L requires compliance as a running annual average (RAA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance dates: Subpart H systems serving ≥10,000 persons comply beginning Jan 1, 2002; serving <10,000 and groundwater-only not under direct influence comply beginning Jan 1, 2004. Best available technology identified: Enhanced coagulation or enhanced softening or GAC10, with chlorine as the primary and residual disinfectant.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCLs for TTHM and HAA5 (Subpart V LRAA compliance and BATs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart V requires locational running annual average (LRAA) compliance for TTHM and HAA5 at each monitoring location; MCLs remain TTHM 0.080 mg/L and HAA5 0.060 mg/L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance dates: LRAA compliance begins on the date specified for subpart V in §141.620(c). Best available technologies for all systems that disinfect source water: enhanced coagulation or enhanced softening, plus GAC10; or nanofiltration with molecular weight cutoff ≤1000 Daltons; or GAC20. For consecutive systems (applies only to disinfected water received): systems serving ≥10,000 persons—improved distribution system and storage tank management to reduce residence time, plus use of chloramines for residual maintenance; systems serving <10,000 persons—improved distribution system and storage tank management to reduce residence time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum residual disinfectant levels (MRDLs)
rubrics_metrics.description: MRDLs are: Chlorine 4.0 mg/L (as Cl2); Chloramines 4.0 mg/L (as Cl2); Chlorine dioxide 0.8 mg/L (as ClO2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance dates: Subpart H systems serving ≥10,000 persons comply beginning Jan 1, 2002; those serving <10,000 and certain groundwater-only systems comply beginning Jan 1, 2004. Administrator identifies control of treatment processes to reduce disinfectant demand and control of disinfection treatment processes to reduce disinfectant levels as the best available means for achieving MRDL compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCL for combined radium-226 and -228
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum contaminant level for combined radium-226 and radium-228 is 5 pCi/L. The combined value is determined by adding results for radium-226 and radium-228 analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCL for gross alpha particle activity (excluding radon and uranium)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum contaminant level for gross alpha particle activity (including radium-226 but excluding radon and uranium) is 15 pCi/L.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCL for beta particle and photon radioactivity (dose-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: The average annual concentration of beta particle and photon radioactivity from man-made radionuclides in drinking water must not produce an annual dose equivalent to the total body or any internal organ greater than 4 millirem/year (mrem/year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as listed in Table A, concentration causing 4 mrem dose equivalents must be calculated on basis of 2 L/day drinking water intake using NBS Handbook 69 168 hour data list. If two or more radionuclides present, the sum of their annual dose equivalents to total body or any organ shall not exceed 4 mrem/year. Table A gives assumed average annual concentrations for tritium (20,000 pCi/L total body) and strontium-90 (8 pCi/L bone marrow) producing 4 mrem/yr.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCL for uranium
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum contaminant level for uranium is 30 µg/L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radionuclides compliance dates and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance dates for combined radium-226/-228, gross alpha, gross beta/photon, and uranium: Community water systems must comply beginning December 8, 2003; compliance determined per §§141.25 and 141.26. Reporting requirements under appendices to subparts O and Q apply on Dec 8, 2003.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best available technologies (BATs) for radionuclides
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator identifies BATs for achieving compliance with radionuclide MCLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table B: Combined radium-226/-228—Ion exchange, reverse osmosis, lime softening. Uranium—Ion exchange, reverse osmosis, lime softening, coagulation/filtration. Gross alpha (excluding radon/uranium)—Reverse osmosis. Beta particle and photon radioactivity—Ion exchange, reverse osmosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small systems compliance technologies for radionuclides (unit techs and limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table C lists unit technologies, operator skill level required, raw water quality range and considerations, and limitations for radionuclide treatment for small systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technologies include ion exchange (IE), point-of-use IE, reverse osmosis (RO), point-of-use RO, lime softening, green sand filtration, co-precipitation with barium sulfate, electrodialysis/EDR, pre-formed hydrous manganese oxide filtration, activated alumina, enhanced coagulation/filtration, etc. Footnotes enumerate limitations (e.g., regeneration solution disposal, need for long-term O&M programs when POU used for compliance, reject water disposal for RO, complexity for lime softening on small systems, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance technologies by system size for radionuclides (Table D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table D maps the suitability of compliance technologies (numbered from Table C) to system size categories (population served): 3,300-10,000; 501-3,300; 25-500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table indicates which numbered technologies (from Table C) are applicable to each contaminant by system size. Note indicates numbers correspond to technologies in Table C of §141.66(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment technique requirement (Subpart H general: 3-log Giardia, 4-log viruses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart H establishes criteria under which filtration is required and treatment technique requirements for surface water and ground water under direct influence of surface water: installing and properly operating water treatment processes which reliably achieve at least 99.9% (3-log) removal/inactivation of Giardia lamblia cysts and at least 99.99% (4-log) removal/inactivation of viruses between a point where raw water is not subject to recontamination and a point downstream before or at the first customer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These treatment technique requirements also serve in lieu of MCLs for Giardia, viruses, HPC bacteria, Legionella, and turbidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance pathways for Subpart H systems (avoid filtration vs filtration)
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system using surface water or ground water under direct influence is in compliance with the Subpart H treatment technique requirements if it either (1) meets avoiding filtration (§141.71) and disinfection requirements (§141.72(a)); or (2) meets filtration requirements (§141.73) and disinfection requirements (§141.72(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified personnel operation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each public water system using a surface water source or ground water under the direct influence must be operated by qualified personnel who meet the requirements specified by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional requirements by system size (subpart P and T)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving at least 10,000 people must also comply with subpart P; systems serving fewer than 10,000 must also comply with subpart T, in addition to Subpart H requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for avoiding filtration—source water quality conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid filtration, a system using a surface water source must meet specified source water quality conditions (and analogous timing rules for GWUDI systems): fecal coliform ≤20/100 ml or total coliform ≤100/100 ml in representative samples immediately prior to first disinfectant application in at least 90% of measurements over previous 6 months of ongoing service; turbidity cannot exceed 5 NTU in representative samples immediately prior to first disinfectant application unless state finds events were unusual and unpredictable and limited in frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a system measures both fecal and total coliforms, the fecal coliform criterion must be met (but not the total coliform criterion). Turbidity exception: state may find events caused by unusual/unpredictable circumstances and count limit is no more than 2 events in past 12 months or no more than 5 events in past 120 months where turbidity >5 NTU. An 'event' is consecutive days with at least one turbidity measurement/day exceeding 5 NTU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for avoiding filtration—site-specific conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Site-specific conditions for avoiding filtration include meeting several disinfection requirements in §141.72 and maintaining watershed and operational safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: meet §141.72(a)(1) at least 11 of 12 previous months (with allowed exceptions for unusual events), meet §141.72(a)(2) at all times, meet §141.72(a)(3) at all times (unless state finds failures were unusual/unpredictable), and meet §141.72(a)(4) on an ongoing basis unless state determines failures not due to treatment deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watershed control program requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems seeking to avoid filtration must maintain a watershed control program minimizing potential for Giardia and virus contamination; the State determines adequacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum the program must: (i) characterize watershed hydrology and land ownership; (ii) identify watershed characteristics/activities that may adversely affect source water quality; (iii) monitor for activities that may adversely affect source water quality. The system must demonstrate control through ownership or written agreements with landowners to control human activities that may affect microbiological quality. The system must submit an annual report identifying special concerns, how they are handled, activities affecting water quality, projected adverse activities, and how the system expects to address them. For GWUDI systems, an approved wellhead protection program under section 1428 may be used if the State deems appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual on-site inspection requirement for watershed and disinfection
rubrics_metrics.description: The public water system must be subject to an annual on-site inspection to assess the watershed control program and disinfection treatment process, conducted by the State or a State-approved party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection must be by competent individuals (sanitary/civil engineers, sanitarians, or technicians experienced in operation/maintenance of public water systems and waterborne disease principles). A report summarizing findings must be prepared yearly. The inspection must include: review of watershed program effectiveness; review of physical condition and protection of source intake; review of equipment maintenance program for low probability of disinfection failure; inspection of disinfection equipment for deterioration; review of operating procedures; review of data records to ensure required tests are conducted/recorded and disinfection effectively practiced; and identification of needed improvements in equipment, maintenance/operation, or data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: No recent waterborne disease outbreak or adequate corrective modification
rubrics_metrics.description: The public water system must not have been identified as a source of a waterborne disease outbreak, or if it has, the system must have been modified sufficiently to prevent another occurrence, as determined by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational compliance history for avoiding filtration (coliforms/E. coli)
rubrics_metrics.description: The system must comply with the MCL for total coliforms (§141.63(a) and (b)) and the MCL for E. coli (§141.63(c)) at least 11 months of the 12 previous months of service, on an ongoing basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may determine that failure to meet this requirement was not caused by a deficiency in treatment of the source water in particular instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trihalomethane/DBP compliance timeline for avoiding filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: The public water system must comply with requirements for trihalomethanes in §§141.12 and 141.30 until Dec 31, 2001; after that date the system must comply with total trihalomethanes, HAA5, bromate, chlorite, chlorine, chloramines, and chlorine dioxide in subpart L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment technique violations for failing to avoid filtration or install filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: A system that fails to meet any one of the criteria in §141.71(a) and (b) (and/or the State has determined filtration is required) and fails to install filtration by the specified date is in violation of a treatment technique requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, a system that has not installed filtration is in violation if (i) turbidity in representative source water sample immediately prior to first/only disinfection exceeds 5 NTU; or (ii) the system is identified as a source of a waterborne disease outbreak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection requirements for systems that do not provide filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-filtering public water systems must provide disinfection treatment sufficient to ensure at least 99.9% (3-log) inactivation of Giardia cysts and 99.99% (4-log) inactivation of viruses every day the system serves water to the public, except any one day each month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each service day the system must calculate CT values from treatment parameters using §141.74(b)(3) and determine if CT is sufficient for required inactivation. If using a disinfectant other than chlorine, the system may demonstrate adequacy to the State via State-approved on-site disinfection challenge studies or other information satisfactory to the State; alternate CT99.9 values or operational parameters may be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundancy/automatic shut-off or auxiliary power for disinfection systems (non-filtered)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disinfection system must have either (i) redundant components, including an auxiliary power supply with automatic start-up and alarm to ensure disinfectant application is maintained continuously while water is delivered; or (ii) automatic shut-off of delivery to distribution system whenever residual disinfectant <0.2 mg/L. If State determines automatic shut-off would cause unreasonable health risk or interfere with fire protection, the system must comply with redundancy option (i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Residual disinfectant entering distribution system minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: The residual disinfectant concentration in the water entering the distribution system cannot be less than 0.2 mg/L for more than 4 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as specified in §141.74(a)(2) and (b)(5) for non-filtered systems; §141.74(a)(2) and (c)(2) for filtered systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residual disinfectant concentration in distribution system detectability limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Residual disinfectant concentration in the distribution system (measured as total chlorine, combined chlorine, or chlorine dioxide) cannot be undetectable in more than 5% of samples each month, for any two consecutive months of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heterotrophic bacteria concentration ≤500/ml (HPC) is deemed to indicate a detectable disinfectant residual for compliance purposes. The regulation provides a formula (with variables a–e) for calculating 'V' which cannot exceed 5% in one month for any two consecutive months. State may exempt systems that cannot have HPC samples transported/analyzed under requisite conditions if State determines the system provides adequate disinfection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection requirements for systems which provide filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: Filtered systems must provide disinfection so that the total treatment processes achieve at least 99.9% (3-log) inactivation/removal of Giardia and at least 99.99% (4-log) inactivation/removal of viruses, as determined by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional filtered-system requirements mirror non-filtered requirements for residual entering distribution (≥0.2 mg/L not for more than 4 hours) and distribution detectability (not undetectable in >5% samples/month for two consecutive months), with the same HPC caveat and State exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration turbidity performance for conventional/direct filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems using conventional or direct filtration, turbidity of representative samples of a system's filtered water must be ≤0.5 NTU in at least 95% of measurements taken each month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured as specified in §141.74(a)(1) and (c)(1). If State determines system can achieve 99.9% Giardia removal/inactivation at some higher turbidity level in ≥95% of measurements each month, the State may substitute that higher turbidity limit for the system.
